newsitem.title: DENMARK: Supreme Court acquits Novo in HIV appeal.
newsitem.headline: Supreme Court acquits Novo in HIV appeal.

text.p: Denmark's Supreme Court on Thursday acquitted biotechnology group Novo Nordisk A/S in an appeal by three haemophiliacs in a blood product case, but ordered the Ministry of Health to pay one of them compensation.

In a statement, the Supreme Court said it had ruled that the state health authorities pay 227,270 crowns ($38,600) in compensation to one of the three haemophiliacs for rejecting a request by doctors to use foreign-screened blood products to treat him in 1985.
The two other haemophiliacs failed to win compensation in their appeal case.

The haemophiliacs appealed in March last year to the Supreme Court against a ruling by a lower Copenhagen court in February 1995 clearing Novo Nordisk of claims that they contracted HIV (human immuno-deficiency virus) that causes AIDS from allegedly unscreened blood products made by the firm.

The case dates back to a mid-1980s scandal involving AIDS-infected blood used in Danish hospital transfusions, centred on blood products manufactured by Nordisk Gentofte, which merged in 1989 with Novo Industri to become Novo Nordisk.

Of the 90 haemophiliacs who contracted HIV and originally sued Novo and the Danish Ministry of Health for compensation, only 34 are still alive today, said the Danish Haemophiliac Association, which mounted the original law suit in 1987.
